videos.title: I Built a Private Netflix for My Whole Family (Self-Hosted + AI Copilot)
videos.description:
I got tired of too many streaming apps, shows that keep disappearing, and ads everywhere. So I built my own private streaming hub for my whole family: a profile for everyone, my own library, new episodes that fetch themselves, and an AI copilot that suggests what to watch but never acts until I confirm.

HomeBot Cinema is open source (a fork of Stremio Web) and runs on a machine you own. Here's the full tour. 👇

⏱️ CHAPTERS
0:00 Why I built this
0:16 Discover: movies, series and anime
0:27 Smart Filters
0:46 Library, calendar and downloads
1:06 Admin panel
1:24 The AI Copilot
2:02 Profiles for the whole family
2:14 Pick a version and press play
2:40 Player: speed, cast and subtitles
3:02 Save to your computer, browse by actor
3:14 Series, auto-download and wrap-up

✨ WHAT YOU'LL SEE
• Smart Filters powered by TMDB: find titles by rating, genre, language and streaming service, with 40 ready-made quick picks
• An AI copilot (Google Gemini) that sees titles only, never names, emails or PINs. It can only suggest and prepare things; nothing happens until you press Confirm
• Separate profiles for everyone at home, each with their own watch history, library and settings
• Pick the version you like by quality or size, and it checks it's ready before you press play
• A player with subtitles, playback speed and casting
• Save movies to your own computer, with quality settings you control
• Auto-download: follow a show and every new episode arrives on its own
• A calendar of upcoming episodes and an admin panel for storage, people and quality

📱 ALSO INCLUDED (not shown in this video)
Optional PIN per profile and a kids profile, and it installs on your phone like an app. Sign-in goes through Cloudflare Access, so only the people you invite get in.

🔧 BUILT WITH
Node.js / Express, SQLite, React (Stremio Web + stremio-core), Docker, Transmission, TMDB, Google Gemini. Narration voice: ElevenLabs.

🔗 LINKS
GitHub: https://github.com/Kanakjr/homebot-cinema
Built on Stremio Web: https://github.com/Stremio/stremio-web

💬 QUESTIONS?
Ask in the comments. I read them all. If you want a deeper video on the AI copilot, auto-download, or the Cloudflare setup, tell me which one.

⚠️ DISCLAIMER
HomeBot Cinema does not host, index or provide any media. It is a client for sources you configure yourself and a manager for your own server. You are responsible for following the laws, licenses and terms of service that apply to you and to the content you use. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Stremio, TMDB, Google or ElevenLabs. Poster images shown belong to their respective owners.

videos.title: I 3D Printed an Adapter to Use DJI Action Filters on My Fujifilm Camera
videos.description:
Why buy another filter kit when you can print an adapter?

I designed a parametric adapter in OpenSCAD that lets me reuse DJI Osmo Action 5 Pro ND/CPL filters on my Fujifilm X-T30 III with the XC13-33mm lens. This video shows the complete process: testing the idea, tuning the fit with calibration rings, reducing vignetting, printing the final adapter, and mounting it on the camera.

Designed in OpenSCAD and printed in PETG on a Bambu Lab A1.

Read the full build story:
https://kanakjr.in/blog/reuse-dji-filters-fujifilm-lens

Gear and tools:
Fujifilm X-T30 III
Fujinon XC13-33mm F3.5-6.3 lens
DJI Osmo Action 5 Pro filter kit
Bambu Lab A1
OpenSCAD with BOSL2

videos.title: 1,200 km through the monsoon · Pune to Goa on a Yamaha XSR 155
videos.description:
Nine days. Twelve hundred kilometres. One monsoon.

A ride from Pune to Goa and back through the Western Ghats
in August 2026, cut down to under five minutes.
No music. Just the engine, the rain, and the road.

Rode down NH-48 through Kolhapur and the Amboli ghat descent,
based five nights on the Goa coast doing daily loops around
Panjim and Anjuna, took one full day inland to Mollem and
Dudhsagar in the middle of the monsoon, and came back up
through Panchgani instead of straight to Pune.

------------------------------------------------

Chapters
0:00  Prologue
0:25  Leaving before the sun
1:15  Somewhere south
1:50  Into the green
3:20  The ride home
4:10  Home

------------------------------------------------

The bike:
Yamaha XSR 155
Air-cooled 155cc single, 6-speed, Variable Valve Actuation

The gear:
Camera: DJI Osmo Action

The route:
Pune · Katraj · Satara · Karad · Kolhapur ·
Nipani · Belgaum · Amboli · Sawantwadi ·
Pernem · Mapusa · Baga

Inside Goa: Candolim, Panjim, Anjuna, Old Goa,
            Mapusa, Ponda, Mollem, Dudhsagar

Back via: Mollem · Belgaum · Kolhapur · Satara ·
Panchgani (overnight) · Shirwal · Katraj · Pune

The numbers (from Google Timeline)
Total distance:      ~1,200 km
Total moving time:    69h 26m
Days on the road:     9
Longest single day:   410 km (outbound day 1)
Longest single leg:   167 km (Mollem to Kolhapur, day 8)

------------------------------------------------

Made with a lot of rain and one very slow film.

videos.title: Hey Jarvis! Building a Custom AI Home Assistant with Gemini Live & DeepAgent
videos.description:
Meet HomeBot, a custom smart home AI assistant powered by Gemini Live for seamless, conversational voice interaction. In this demo, I show how HomeBot integrates directly with the physical environment to control smart lights, report on room sensors (like temperature and air quality), and monitor ongoing 3D prints in real-time.

Beyond basic smart home controls, HomeBot uses a custom "deepagent" architecture to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Watch as it autonomously fetches movie recommendations, checks the existing media library, and delegates download tasks completely hands-free.

videos.title: HomeBot AI: The Ultimate Smart Home AI (Home Assistant, Gemini, LangChain Deepagent & Ollama)
videos.description:
Welcome to a walkthrough of HomeBot AI, a custom project I've been developing to solve the fragmentation in my home automation setup. Between Home Assistant entities, Sonarr/Radarr for media management, network tracking, and monitoring prints on my Bambu Lab A1, there was no single, aggregated way to control everything.

Enter HomeBot AI: A unified dashboard powered by a LangChain DeepAgent, leveraging Gemini Flash 2.5 for complex tasks and local offline models like Qwen via Ollama for privacy-focused, zero-cost tasks like AI summaries.

In this video, I demonstrate how HomeBot AI brings generative UI widgets, automated media downloading, intelligent agent memory, automated video transcoding, and power analytics all under one roof.

Links & Resources:
• GitHub Repository: https://github.com/Kanakjr/homebot
• HomeBot Documentation & Architecture: https://kanakjr.github.io/homebot/

Timestamps:

videos.title: YAMAHA XSR 155: Konkan Costal Ride
videos.description:
Just wrapped up a soul-satisfying 800 km trip over the long weekend. The route took me from Pune to Harihareshwar, then down the coast to Ratnagiri, and finally back home.

The Ride Experience:
The bike was buttery smooth throughout the Konkan twisties. I was honestly surprised by the efficiency. I managed to clock an average of 50 kmpl, which is phenomenal given the varied terrain.

The Ergonomics:
If there’s one gripe, it’s the handlebar position. By the time I hit the 600 km mark, I started feeling some strain in my shoulders. The stance is slightly aggressive for long hudistance touring, but it was nothing a few stretches and short breaks couldn't fix. It’s manageable, but something to keep in mind if you plan on back-to-back 300km+ days.

Final Verdict:
I absolutely love this machine. It’s got character, looks gorgeous in the wild (shot this near Ganpatipule), and holds its own on the highway.

Ride Stats:
Total Distance: 800 km
Route: Pune  Harihareshwar - Ganpatipule - Ratnagiri - Pune
Mileage: ~51 kmpl
Comfort: 7/10 (Shoulder strain is real)
Fun Factor: 11/10
